_comment: RU verb paradigms v1. Key=EN template token. present=[I,you,he,she,they,it]

is.cop._comment: Task 6.5: explicit pure-copula sense, identical paradigm to 'is'. New translations that specifically mean 'to be [adjective/noun]' (not 'to be about to X') should prefer this key over the overloaded plain 'is' so intent is unambiguous in the source text; existing '[is]' usages are untouched.

is.aux._comment: Task 6.5: 'to be going to / to be about to' auxiliary sense. Unlike 'is'/'is.cop' this is a REAL present-tense verb ('собираться'), not an omitted copula -- English 'is going to demolish' needs an actual Russian verb, not silence.

has.obj._comment: Task 6.5: explicit 'owns a physical object' sense, identical paradigm to 'has' ('имеет лом' = has a crowbar). New translations that specifically mean object-possession should prefer this key over the overloaded plain 'has'; existing '[has]' usages are untouched.

has.qual._comment: Task 6.5: 'has a quality/attribute' sense (e.g. 'has poor piloting skills'). Russian expresses this idiom as 'U <genitive pronoun> <noun phrase>' (у тебя плохие навыки), a possessive prepositional phrase, NOT a conjugated verb -- there is no Russian verb slot to fill at the '[has.qual]' token position at all. Modeled as an omit-present copula (kind=copula, omitPresent=true, like 'is'/'is.cop') so VerbPrefix silently drops the token and absorbs the preceding space, exactly like it already does for a dropped 'is' copula. CONVENTION for Task 6.7: the translator writes the 'У [us-gen]' possessive phrase directly in the surrounding RU sentence themselves, BEFORE the '[has.qual]' token; '[has.qual]' itself renders nothing and exists only so the token still parses/dispatches to GrammarUtils.Verb (routing through dictVerbs) instead of falling through as an unrecognized literal. Example: EN '[us] [has.qual] poor piloting skills.' -> RU 'У [us-gen] [has.qual] плохие навыки пилотирования.' -> 'У тебя плохие навыки пилотирования.'
